title: Block-by-Block Optimization Stages — Variable S/F + Wear + Thermal Tracking
description: Wire Phase 2 (block-by-block optimization) into the pipeline. This is where PRISM differentiates from every other post processor — instead of constant S/F per tool, every G-code line gets individually optimized based on instantaneous engagement, chip thinning, corner detection, wear progression, and cumulative thermal state. Uses InstantaneousEngagementEngine, EngagementAdaptiveFeedEngine, StochasticToolWearEngine, ToolpathThermalEngine, and StochasticDeflectionEngine.

units.title: Stage 2.1-2.2 — Engagement analysis + Chip thinning compensation per block
steps: Wire InstantaneousEngagementEngine.computeOptimalSF() as pipeline stage
For each cutting block: calculate ae (radial depth), ap (axial depth), engagement angle θ
For ball end mills: calculate D_eff = 2√(2Rap - ap²), adjust RPM to maintain Vc at effective diameter
Chip thinning: when ae < D/2, actual chip thickness h < fz. Compensate: fz_adj = fz × (D / (2 × √(ae × (D-ae))))
Store per-block engagement data in ToolpathBlock for downstream stages
Classify each block: rapid/air/light/nominal/heavy/corner/slotting
exit_conditions: Every cutting block has ae, ap, θ, D_eff computed
Chip thinning factor ≥ 1.0 for all ae ≤ D/2 (invariant)
Ball end mill D_eff monotonically increases with ap (invariant)
Feed increases proportionally to chip thinning factor

units.title: Stage 2.3-2.5 — Adaptive feed modes + Corner/plunge detection
steps: Wire EngagementAdaptiveFeedEngine: select mode based on optimization target
Constant chip load mode: maintain fz regardless of engagement changes
Constant force mode: maintain Fc by adjusting feed as engagement changes (Kienzle model)
Constant MRR mode: maintain volumetric removal rate across varying engagement
Constant thermal mode: maintain tool-chip interface temperature (Loewen-Shaw)
Corner detection: when engagement angle spikes >120° at direction changes, reduce feed by engagement ratio
Plunge detection: Z-dominant moves get 50% feed reduction (axial cutting is weaker)
Ramp detection: helical/ramp entry gets graduated feed increase
Small arc detection: arcs with R < 3×tool_diameter get curvature-limited feed
exit_conditions: Constant chip load mode produces uniform fz across varying ae
Corner feed reduction prevents engagement spikes >150%
Plunge moves correctly identified and derated
Ramp entries show smooth feed ramp-up

units.title: Stage 2.6-2.8 — Wear progression + Thermal tracking + Deflection-limited feed
steps: Wire StochasticToolWearEngine: Takeyama-Murata flank wear ODE — VB(t) progresses through program
Block-by-block wear accumulation: each block's cutting time adds to cumulative wear state
When VB approaches limit (0.3mm roughing, 0.15mm finishing), reduce speed by 10-20% to extend life
Proactive tool change advisory: predict remaining life, suggest tool change point for multi-pass operations
Wire ToolpathThermalEngine: cumulative heat tracking — deep pockets accumulate thermal energy
After N consecutive cutting blocks, if cumulative_heat > threshold, inject dwell or reduce speed
Wire StochasticDeflectionEngine: per-block force → deflection check against tolerance
Blocks where force produces deflection > tolerance/3 get feed reduction
For thin-wall machining: track workpiece stiffness degradation as material is removed
exit_conditions: Wear state increases monotonically through program
S/F derate activates when VB > 70% of limit
Thermal accumulation produces measurable speed differences between block 1 and block 50 of a deep pocket
Deflection-limited blocks are flagged with force and deflection values
